scope: Read-only research of kernel and transport components for indexed input embedding gradients. No source edits, installs, GPU execution or measured speedup.

repositories.name: NVIDIA/cuEmbed
findings: Compressed EmbeddingBackward produces unique-row gradients and inverse mapping.
Current support matrix specifies FP32/FP16 and a single GPU; BF16 and multiple devices are future work.
PyTorch example returns dense gradients despite kernel compressed-output capability. Fake registrations exist.

hopper_evidence.workload: Forward embedding-bag sum,10M categories,widths32/64/128,hotness64; not distributed backward and not our D4096.
hopper_evidence.use: Hardware and kernel reference only; cannot estimate the5.2ms tail.

repositories.name: deepseek-ai/DeepEP
findings: EngramBuffer has write and fetch with per-layer wait hooks for GPU/CPU BF16/FP8 remote data.
No backward gradient push/reduce API in inspected EngramBuffer.
Experimental current feature requires CUDA13.1+ and Hopper+; recorded training baseline CUDA13.0 and earlier DeepEP1.2.1.

repositories.name: deepseek-ai/Engram
findings: Official released code is a demonstration mocking ordinary components; not an integrated distributed training implementation.

shape_bounds.limits: Balanced row ownership is an assumption. Unique row counts, skew, padding, pack/unpack and protocol overhead are unmeasured. Dense input is not wire traffic. Sparse all-gather has different cost than owner-directed exchange. BF16 transport is lossless only after native local BF16 duplicate coalescing; widen before FP32 owner SUM and FP32 accumulation.

torchrec_fbgemm.pattern: RwSequenceEmbeddingSharding with row-owner input routing and inverse autograd SequenceEmbeddingsAllToAll. DENSE selects BatchedDenseEmbedding backed by DenseTableBatchedEmbeddingBagsCodegen, not plain nn.Embedding.
blockers: Generated CUDA backward max_embedding_dim=2048 and checked for DENSE/FUSED non-index-select paths. Our D4096 exceeds it.
Inspected weight/cache dispatcher accepts Float/Half/FP8 weights but not BF16 weights; BF16 output/gradient support is separate.
FP32 external dense AdamW, microbatch accumulation, scaling, EMA and GFSDP ownership need integration.

hopper_benchmark.limitation: Not our single D4096 table or gradient-tail-only benchmark. No transfer of this ratio to our throughput.
